app.title: Geogenesis
app.subtitle: a planet simulation
climate.aria: Monthly climate diagram: mean annual temperature {temperature} degrees Celsius and annual precipitation {precipitation} millimetres
controls.startHint: Choose how early in the planet's history to begin
startHelp.young: 0.5 billion years old: a hot, lifeless world with a faint young Sun, small continents and declining bombardment.
startHelp.microbial: 2 billion years old: an anoxic ocean already inhabited by prokaryotes.
startHelp.quick: 4 billion years old: the former starting state, with prokaryotes and eukaryotes approaching.
layer.label: Map layer
map.label: Planet map; scroll to zoom, drag to move a zoomed map, with a tool selected, click to use it
map.globeLabel: Planet globe; drag to turn it, with a tool selected, click to use it
map.zoomIn: Zoom in (+ or the mouse wheel)
map.minimap: Show or hide the minimap of the whole planet when zoomed in or on the globe (M)
map.minimapLabel: Minimap of the whole planet; click or drag to move the view
view.label: View
tools.title: Tools
tools.hint: Pick a tool, then click the map.
tools.noEnergy: Not enough energy for that tool.
tools.notAllowed: That tool cannot be used there.
toolHelp.raise: Lifts the land around the clicked point by up to 500 m.
toolHelp.lower: Lowers the land around the clicked point by up to 500 m.
toolHelp.volcano: Raises a volcanic peak and releases CO₂.
toolHelp.meteor: Blasts a crater and devastates life around it.
toolHelp.seedLife: Places a life class that has evolved before where it can live.
toolHelp.monolith: Awakens intelligence in the most promising animal nearby, or advances an existing civilization.
toolHelp.addCo2: Adds 200 ppm of CO₂ to the atmosphere.
toolHelp.removeCo2: Removes half of the atmosphere's CO₂.
toolHelp.earthquake: Drag to choose a push direction. The crust rises into a mountain range across the push and nearby settlements are damaged.
toolHelp.hurricane: Drives a damaging cyclone from the clicked sea or coast along the surface wind.
toolHelp.tidalWave: Sends a tsunami from the clicked ocean cell onto surrounding low coasts.
toolHelp.fire: Burns land vegetation and animals in the brush and adds a little soot.
disasters.title: Disasters
disasterHelp.earthquakes: Natural earthquakes at plate boundaries; convergent margins are strongest.
disasterHelp.tsunamis: Tsunamis from large submarine earthquakes and ocean impacts.
disasterHelp.cyclones: Tropical cyclones fed by warm seas and carried towards downwind coasts.
disasterHelp.droughts: Recurring drought lowers food capacity in semi-arid and strongly seasonal regions.
disasterHelp.dustStorms: Dry, bare and windy land supplies a small atmospheric dust load.
disasterHelp.impacts: Natural asteroid and comet impacts; player meteor tools are unaffected.
disasterHelp.supervolcanoes: Rare large eruptions and large igneous provinces; ordinary volcanism continues.
controlsPanel.title: Model controls
controlsPanel.sliderHint: {description}. Double-click to reset; type a value.
controlsPanel.resetAllHint: Reset every control in this window to its default
window.geosphereHint: Open or close the Geosphere controls (E)
window.atmosphereHint: Open or close the Atmosphere controls (A)
window.biosphereHint: Open or close the Biosphere controls (B)
window.planetHint: Open or close the Planet details (D)
window.centreHint: Centre this window on the simulation stage
event.lifeOrigin: Life originated in a hydrothermal ocean
event.runawayWarning: The planet is nearing a runaway greenhouse
event.runawayEnded: The steam atmosphere rained out and oceans returned
event.oceansLost: The planet lost its oceans to space
event.stagnantLid: Plate tectonics stopped and a stagnant lid formed
event.atmosphereLost: The planet lost nearly all of its atmosphere
event.methaneRelease: Rapid warming released a vast store of methane
event.tsunami: A tsunami struck a settled coast
event.drought: A major drought gripped the civilization
civ.title: Civilization
civ.afterExodus: The civilization left the planet at {age}. Another species may yet become sentient.
events.title: Events
events.centreHint: Centre the map and globe on this event
event.massExtinction: Mass extinction: most complex life died out ({name})
event.cambrianExplosion: Cambrian explosion: the first animals appeared and began to diversify
extinctionCause.dust: darkness from dust in the air
extinctionCause.oxygen: too little or too much oxygen
event.exodus: Exodus: {name} left the planet for the stars
life.title: Life
legend.label: Map legend
legend.mapIcons: Life and city icons visible on the map
controls.stepHint: Advance the simulation by one step (S)
controls.speedHint: How fast the simulation runs; Fast runs as quickly as your computer allows
controls.saveHint: Download this planet as a file
controls.resolutionHint: Finer grids show more detail but run more slowly.
scenarioHelp.random: An evolving rocky planet. Choose whether to begin before life, with microbes, or near complex life.
scenarioHelp.daisyworld: Lovelock's thought experiment: black and white daisies keep a planet comfortable as its star brightens.
scenarioHelp.aquarium: A water world with no continents, only the islands that volcanoes build.
scenarioHelp.mars: Present-day Mars: cold, dry, thin-aired, unmagnetized and geologically stagnant.
scenarioHelp.venus: Present-day Venus: a hot, dry, slowly retrograde world beneath a massive CO₂ atmosphere.
scenarioHelp.brighteningSun: Keep an old, living Earth habitable as its aging Sun brightens toward a runaway greenhouse.
scenarioHelp.snowball: Thaw a globally frozen microbial planet and keep its new climate stable.
scenarioHelp.cradle: Guide an evolving biosphere until one of its species becomes sentient.
planet.radiusHint: Planet radius in kilometres; gravity follows Earth-like density unless a preset overrides it
planet.distanceHint: Average distance from the star in astronomical units
planet.starTypeHint: F stars are bright and short-lived; K and M stars are dimmer and longer-lived
planet.rotationHint: Sidereal day in hours; use a negative value for retrograde rotation
planet.moonHint: A large moon keeps axial tilt stable; without one it wanders chaotically
planet.waterHint: Water inventory in metres of global-equivalent layer; leave blank to fit the generated basin datum
planet.landTargetHint: Desired ice-free land area on a mature planet; the simulation adds submerged continental shelf when deriving its crust target
planet.title: Planet
stat.ageHint: Planet age (or calendar year once a civilization runs in years)
stat.stepHint: Simulated time covered by one step
stat.temperatureHint: Mean surface air temperature (Earth today: about 15 °C)
stat.co2Hint: Atmospheric carbon dioxide; more CO₂ means a warmer planet (Earth before industry: 280 ppm)
stat.pressureHint: Total atmospheric surface pressure (Earth: about 1 bar)
stat.o2Hint: Atmospheric oxygen as percent of air and partial pressure; animals need enough oxygen pressure (Earth: 21% and 0.21 bar)
stat.iceHint: Share of the surface covered by ice
stat.seaLevelHint: Sea level relative to the ice-free planet; water stored in land ice lowers it
stat.sunHint: Brightness of the star relative to the Sun today; stars brighten as they age
stat.runawayMarginHint: Headroom below the wet-atmosphere radiation limit; below 15 W/m2 warns that a runaway greenhouse is close
stat.energyHint: Energy for tools; it builds up over time
stat.computeHint: Computer time the last step took
layerHelp.terrain: Elevation, oceans, rivers, lakes and ice
layerHelp.plates: Tectonic plates; they drift and build mountains where they collide
layerHelp.volcanism: Subduction arcs, spreading ridges, continental rifts and mantle hotspots
layerHelp.seasons: Amplitude of the seasonal monthly-mean temperature cycle
layerHelp.pressure: Sea-level pressure, with highs, lows and 4 hPa isobars
layerHelp.precipitation: Annual rain and snow, carried by the winds from the sea
layerHelp.biomes: Biomes set by temperature and aridity, shaded by actual plant cover
layerHelp.life: The most advanced life in each place
layerHelp.diversity: How many life classes share each place
layerHelp.hazard: Combined long-term earthquake, tsunami, cyclone and drought risk to people
layerHelp.daisies: Cover of black and white daisies
layerHelp.oceanOxygen: Dissolved surface-ocean oxygen relative to saturation; red water is anoxic
layerHelp.nutrients: Surface-ocean phosphate supply relative to the modern mean
layerHelp.clathrates: Methane stored in cold land, permafrost and shallow continental shelves
viewHelp.map: The whole planet as a flat map
viewHelp.globe: The planet as a globe; drag to turn it
panel.label: Planet details
help.keyView: Switch between the flat map and the globe
help.keyEscape: Put the tool down, close this window
help.mouse: Hover over the map to inspect a place. Scroll to zoom the map and drag to move it. On the globe, drag to turn it.
controlHelp.solarFactor: Brightness of the star; a brighter star warms the planet
controlHelp.obliquity: Axial tilt sets the contrast between summer and winter
controlHelp.volcanism: Volcanic activity; volcanoes release CO₂ and build islands
controlHelp.driftSpeed: How fast the tectonic plates move
controlHelp.erosion: How fast rain and rivers wear down mountains
controlHelp.mutationRate: How quickly new life classes evolve
controlHelp.greenhouse: Strength of the greenhouse effect of CO₂, methane and water vapour
controlHelp.cloudAlbedo: How strongly low clouds reflect sunlight
controlHelp.surfaceAlbedo: Reflectivity of ice-free land and sea
controlHelp.airSeaHeat: How fast temperatures follow the ocean; higher means less thermal lag
controlHelp.rainfall: Evaporation and rainfall intensity of the water cycle
controlHelp.advanceRate: Overall pace of life: its origin and the evolution of new classes
controlHelp.reproduction: How fast populations grow and shrink towards what the land can support
controlHelp.thermalTolerance: How wide a temperature range life can tolerate
stat.eraHint: Each era runs at its own pace: 2 million years per step while only microbes live, 500,000 years once complex life evolves, then centuries to a few years per step as a civilization advances.
layerHelp.wind: Surface wind speed; the arrows show where it blows
layerHelp.oceanCurrents: Warm and cold currents: how much warmer or colder the sea surface is than the latitude would make it
overlay.label: Map overlays
overlayHelp.wind: Show wind arrows over any map layer
overlayHelp.currents: Show ocean current arrows over any map layer
overlayHelp.isobars: Show 4 hPa pressure contours and high/low centres over any map layer
overlayHelp.icons: Show the dominant life class or city at regularly spaced places
help.keyOverlay: Show or hide wind, current, isobar, life and city overlays
help.keyWindows: Open or close the model and planet windows
help.keyZoom: Zoom the map in or out
layerHelp.clouds: Cloud cover: thick where air rises and rains, stratus over cold seas, clear skies over deserts
temperatureMonth.label: Shown temperature
temperatureMonth.hint: Show the annual mean or a representative January or July monthly mean
goal.title: Goal
goal.briefing.brighteningSun: The Sun keeps brightening: weathering is starving the air of CO₂, land life is thinning, and a runaway greenhouse will boil the oceans near 7 billion years. Preserve liquid oceans and complex life until the planet is 8.1 billion years old. Sunshades can dim sunlight by at most 8%; cloud and surface controls have modest ranges.
goal.briefing.snowball: This world is locked beneath global ice. Use CO₂, volcanism and albedo to bring ice below 15% and temperature above 5 °C, then hold both for 5 million years. You have 1 billion years.
goal.briefing.cradle: Nurture this microbial world through complex evolution until a species becomes sentient. Complex-life extinction or a two-billion-year delay ends the attempt.
goal.keepPlayingHint: Continue this planet as a sandbox after the outcome
goal.newPlanetHint: Open the menu to start another planet
goal.reason.oceansLost: The oceans were lost to space.
goal.reason.survivedBrightening: Liquid oceans and complex life survived the brightening Sun.
goal.reason.snowballThawed: The global ice retreated and the warm climate remained stable.
goal.briefing.terraformMars: Mars is cold, dry and nearly airless. Build CO₂ and nitrogen generators to thicken the air, drop ice meteors for water, add oxygen and a biome factory for plants. Reach 0.5 bar, 5 °C, open sea and growing plants, and hold them for 10 million years. You have 500 million years; impacts and eruptions destroy devices.
goal.reason.terraformed: The planet became warm, wet and green, and stayed that way.
scenarioHelp.terraformMars: Goal: make present-day Mars habitable with generators, ice meteors and a biome factory.
toolHelp.iceMeteor: Drops a ~200 km icy comet: a crater and about 10 m of global water on an Earth-sized planet, more on a small one.
toolHelp.co2Generator: Builds a factory that keeps releasing CO₂ (about 0.01 bar per million years on Earth).
toolHelp.n2Generator: Builds a factory that keeps releasing nitrogen (about 0.01 bar per million years on Earth).
toolHelp.o2Generator: Builds a factory that keeps releasing oxygen; without life it slowly reacts away again.
toolHelp.co2Scrubber: Builds a plant that turns atmospheric CO₂ into rock (about 0.5 bar per million years), stopping at 280 ppm.
toolHelp.biomeFactory: Builds a factory that keeps sowing land plants nearby wherever they can grow.
stat.lifeHint: What a distant telescope would see: oxygen and methane together reveal life; one alone is only a hint
scenarioHelp.stoneAge: Goal: lead a young stone-age people from one island through every age to Exodus.
scenarioHelp.cambrian: An Earth-like planet as the Cambrian begins: animals in the seas, bare land. No goal.
goal.briefing.exodus: A people of mammals has just become sentient on one island. Help them spread, survive plagues and wars, and advance through all seven ages until they leave the planet. A collapse of the civilization or 300,000 years without Exodus ends the attempt.
goal.reason.exodus: The civilization left the planet in an Exodus.
